question.problem:
Let $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ be a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{rank}(T)=\text{nullity}(T)=3$

II. If $v=[1,0,0]^{T}$ is a solution of $T(x)=0$ then $T$ is invertible.

III. If there is not $u\in {R}^{3}$ such that $T(u)=[1,0,0]^{T},$ then $\text{rank}(T)=3.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{3}$ into ${R}^{3},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=3 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)=\{0\} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T)=3.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. According to the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T) & =3-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =3-3 \\  & =0 \\  & \ne 3.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $v$ is a solution of $T(x)=0$, we have that $T(v)=0.$ Therefore $v\in \text{Ker}(T),$ thus according to the invertible matrix theorem $T$ is not invertible.

- Statement III is false. Since there is not $u\in {R}^{3}$ such that $T(u)=[1,0,0]^{T},$ we have that $T$ is not  a bijection (an invertible transformation). According to the invertible matrix theorem, $\text{rank}(T)\ne 3.$

Therefore, the correct option is "None of the statements are true."

choices.value: None of the statements are true
